title: Crosswalk: Cache Heuristics Harmonization & Operator Knowledge Transfer
author: Marta Liu
body:
Summary:

This retrospective documents a three-month cross-team program ("Crosswalk") to harmonize cache eviction and prefetch heuristics across the platform, plus the accompanying operator knowledge transfer and playbook updates. The goal was to reduce SLO volatility driven by heuristic drift across schedulers, reduce token-cost variance, and make on-call actions reproducible.

Background and motivation:

- Problem: Multiple teams had independently tuned runtime cache and prefetch heuristics (edge prefetch, KV-prefix warmset, tenant warmset thresholds). Over time small local changes resulted in inconsistent behavior during bursts: some regions aggressively prefetched, driving unexpected token cost and cold-cache misses elsewhere.
- Impact observed: 2.8% median increase in 95th-percentile token latency for multi-tenant inference during the November surge; token-cost spikes (single-day delta) up to 14% for a subset of tenants on mixed workloads.
- Scope: runtime scheduling, platform prefetch layer, operator runbooks, and dashboards/alerts. Not in scope: model architecture or serving kernel-level changes.

Timeline of Crosswalk program:

1. 2026-08-12: Incident trigger — regional latency spike flagged by SLO burn monitor.
2. 2026-08-18: Working group chartered (Platform runtime, Serving, SRE, Observability).
3. 2026-09 to 2026-10: Inventory phase — collect heuristics, config, and operator runbooks.
4. 2026-11: Harmonization trial (canary in eu-west-1 then us-west-2).
5. 2026-11-15: Retrospective draft (this doc created).
6. 2026-12: Cross-team training sessions and runbook updates.
7. 2027-01-10: Finalized action items and dashboard templates.

Key findings:

- Divergent defaults: Four services used different default warmset retention windows (10s, 30s, 60s, 120s). The shortest window caused thrash during noisy bursts.
- Priority mismatch: Tenant-priority scoring was being applied inconsistently; some delegating components treated score >= 70 as burst-capable while others used >= 85.
- Operator mental model gap: On-call runbooks documented manual prefills for cold-cache incidents, but the procedures were ambiguous and differed by region.
- Observability blind spots: Existing dashboards showed aggregate warmset hit-rate but not by tenant class and workload fingerprint (chat vs. embeddings).

Quantified impact (post-canary measurements):

- eu-west-1 canary (harmonized heuristics): 95th P99 token latency decreased from 420 ms to 360 ms (-14.3%).
- Token-cost variance across tenants (sampled cohort): coefficient of variation down from 0.22 to 0.12.
- Operator time-to-diagnosis for cache-related incidents: median reduced from 28 minutes to 11 minutes.

Decisions made:

- Standardize a conservative baseline for warmset retention: default = 60s, tenant-class overrides allowed with explicit review.
- Adopt a single tenant-priority scale (0-100) and canonical thresholding: burst-capable = >= 80.
- Add a "graceful backoff" circuit inside prefetcher: exponential backoff up to 5 minutes when warmset thrash detected.
- Treat heuristics changes as "config-feature" releases requiring canary and observability checklist signoff.

Action items and rollout plan (owners and dates):

1) Publish canonical heuristics spec and config table (owner: Platform runtime team — Maya Santos) — due 2027-01-31.

2) Dashboard templates (owner: Observability — Evan Chen) — create 3 panels and an alert:
   - Panel A: warmset hit-rate by tenant-class (last 30d window).
   - Panel B: prefetch-trigger rate and backoff events (per region).
   - Panel C: token-cost variance histogram (per-tenant daily).
   - Alert: >= 15% reduction in warmset hit-rate for > 5 min for >= 5 tenants in same shard.
   Example Datadog query (sample):
   "avg:llm.prefetch.hit_rate{environment:prod,region:eu-west-1}.rollup(avg,3600) by {tenant_class} < 0.65"

3) Runbook harmonization (owner: SRE/Oncall — Diego Ramirez) — migrate and consolidate duplicate pages into: /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/crosswalk-prefetch-and-warmset-runbook-2027.json — due 2027-02-14. Steps will include:
   a) Pre-incident checklist (what metrics to collect).
   b) Operator remediation steps (order-of-operations for manual warmfill, prefills, and soft-evictions).
   c) Post-remediation validation queries.

4) Operator training and exercises (owner: Platform learning lead — Priya Nair) — run three 90-minute labs covering:
   - Lab 1: Identifying warmset thrash and isolating the offending tenant.
   - Lab 2: Safe manual-prefill and rollback.
   - Lab 3: Interpreting dashboard panels and handoff notes.
   Schedule: one session per fortnight starting 2027-02-21.

5) Canary policy update and automation (owner: Serving runtime — Jacob O'Connor) — implement automated canary guardrails to ensure observability checklist completion before heuristics config promotion — due 2027-03-07.

Monitoring and acceptance criteria:

- SLO: Maintain 95th-percentile token latency target (global) <= baseline_pre_crosswalk + 3% for 30 days post-rollout.
- Cost: No >10% sustained token-cost uplift for any tenant cohort for 14 days post-change.
- Operator efficiency: median time-to-detect and time-to-diagnose remain <= 15 minutes for cache-related incidents.

Runbook extracts (operator quick-reference):

- Quick triage checklist:
  1. Check warmset hit-rate by tenant_class -> panel A.
  2. If hit-rate < 0.6 for > 5 minutes, check prefetch-trigger rate -> panel B.
  3. Correlate tenant fingerprint (chat vs. embedding) using request_label parsed traces.
  4. If thrash confirmed, apply soft backoff toggle (ui/infra flag) and observe for 3 minutes.
  5. If no improvement, perform manual warmfill for impacted warmset shard (follow manual-prefill substeps).

- Manual-prefill substeps (operator):
  1) Identify top 5 requests for shard using sampling query.
  2) Run prefill-hydrate command (cli):
     ./platform-prefill --shard <shard-id> --requests-file requests.json --concurrency 4 --dry-run=false
  3) Monitor token-latency and warmset hit-rate; revert if error rate > 0.5% or latency increases.

Lessons learned and recommendations:

- Governance beats heroics: consistent defaults and release gates prevent asymmetric tuning.
- Observability is granular: aggregate metrics hide tenant-level pathologies; always sample and tag by fingerprint.
- Invest in operator pedagogy: short labs with scenario-based playbooks were the most effective way to close knowledge gaps.

Appendix A — Canonical heuristics table (excerpt):

| Component                | Default | Rationale                          | Override scope      | Owner          |
|-------------------------|---------|------------------------------------|---------------------|----------------|
| Warmset retention       | 60s     | Balance cold miss vs. memory churn | tenant-class only   | Platform runtime|
| Prefetch concurrency    | 8       | Prevent requester overload         | region-level only   | Serving runtime |
| Backoff multiplier      | 2x      | Fast graceful reduction of thrash  | global only         | Platform runtime|
| Tenant priority burst   | >= 80  | Clear burst-capable threshold      | tenant exceptions   | Product/Revenue |

Appendix B — Checklist for config-feature release:

- [ ] Spec published and reviewed by runtime + serving + observability.
- [ ] Canary plan documented (regions, sampling fraction, rollback criteria).
- [ ] Dashboards deployed and alerting wired to oncall.
- [ ] Operator lab scheduled and recording archived.

Appendix C — Links & artifacts:

- Inventory spreadsheet (internal link): platform-cache-inventory-2026.csv
- Canary experiment notebook: /notebooks/harmonize-prefetch-canary-2026.ipynb
- Training slides: /assets/platform-training/crosswalk-prefetch-2026.pdf

Acknowledgements:

Thanks to all contributors from Platform runtime, Serving, Observability, Product, and SRE who participated in the Crosswalk program. This retrospective is intended as a stable reference for future heuristics alignment efforts.
